questions.question: What are the three main reasons firms buy the ESource white-label bookkeeping tool?
choices: Their brand, data stays home, and lower cost per client
Bank feeds, payroll integration, and mobile app access
Client login portal, live bank feeds, and unlimited users
Free trial period, 24/7 support, and automatic tax filing
questions.feedback_correct: Exactly—those three reasons are what wins deals and should roll off your tongue in one breath.
questions.feedback_incorrect: While some of those features are valuable, the three core buying reasons are their brand on reports, client data staying on their computers, and lower per-client cost. Review Slide 3 to see how these three reasons set us apart.

questions.question: Which discovery question should you ask first when talking to a potential firm?
choices: How many hours a month do you spend chasing clients about transactions?
Which software are your clients on, and who pays for it?
Whose name do your clients see when they get their reports?
How did this year's price increases hit you and your clients?
questions.feedback_correct: Starting with today's tools sets the stage and helps you understand their current situation before moving into cost and brand.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The discovery questions have a specific order: start with today's tools, then move to cost, then brand, then time. This order builds naturally from their current situation to their pain points.

questions.question: In the demo, what should you show immediately after uploading a bank statement?
choices: The Health dashboard colors and the P and L report
The Ask Client tab with grouped questions
The Bank Check tab to prove the numbers tie to the bank
The Status tab showing missing client statements in red
questions.feedback_correct: The Bank Check tab showing "Ties" proves the math and builds confidence that the upload worked correctly.
questions.feedback_incorrect: While those other screens are part of the demo, the immediate next step after upload is to prove the numbers match the bank using the Bank Check tab. This builds credibility early.

questions.question: How many staff seats does the firm pay for when they license the ESource tool?
choices: One seat per staff member, at $10 per seat per month
Seats are unlimited, so no additional charge for adding people
Up to five seats included, then $5 per additional seat
One seat per client book, up to the size of their firm
questions.feedback_correct: That's right—pricing is per active client book only, and unlimited staff can use the system without extra cost.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The pricing model charges per active client book, not per staff member. Unlimited staff seats means firms don't worry about adding people, which is a real selling point.

questions.question: What is the correct way to calculate the monthly price for a firm with 38 client books?
choices: Use the calculator at esourcebookkeeper.com/calculator and type 38
Multiply 38 by $17 and round down to the nearest dollar
Use the Competitor Battle Cards to cross-reference the tier
Add $20 + $17 + $15 + $14 + $13 and divide by 38
questions.feedback_correct: Never do the math by hand—always open the calculator tool so you get the graduated tier math right every time.
questions.feedback_incorrect: While the tiers are real, doing the math manually is error-prone. The calculator at esourcebookkeeper.com/calculator handles the graduated pricing correctly: $20 for book one, $17 for books 2–10, $15 for books 11–30, and $14 for books 31–38.

questions.question: When a firm says "Our clients know QuickBooks," what is the best response?
choices: Agree that QuickBooks is the industry standard and offer to integrate with it
Explain that clients get Excel reports with the firm's name and don't need to learn new software
Suggest they train their clients on the ESource interface over a few weeks
Offer a discount if they commit to switching all clients immediately
questions.feedback_correct: That's the right objection handler—clients receive professional Excel reports with the firm's brand, so they never have to log into or learn any new software.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The key insight is that client familiarity with QuickBooks isn't a barrier because our reports come out as Excel files with the firm's name on them. Clients don't need to use or learn any software.

questions.question: What is the key security message you should tell an owner who worries about an employee leaving with client data?
choices: ESource encrypts all data with military-grade algorithms that no one can break
Only people the owner adds can sign in, and when they leave, their access locks the books immediately
The firm must sign a legal non-compete agreement with every employee
All backups are stored in a secure cloud vault that ESource controls
questions.feedback_correct: That's the core security story—access is controlled entirely by the owner, and removal is instant and device-wide, so client data stays theirs.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The winning security message is about the owner's control: they add and remove people, and removal locks the books immediately on every device, even lost laptops. That's what keeps clients truly safe.

questions.question: What should you propose as the scope and duration of the pilot when closing a deal?
choices: All client books for 90 days to see full impact across the firm
One client book for 30 days to minimize risk and setup time
Three to five clients for 60 days, running alongside their current system
A full migration of 50% of clients for 120 days with a money-back guarantee
questions.feedback_correct: Exactly—a small, low-risk pilot of a few clients for two months proves value without asking them to abandon their current system.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The pilot strategy is designed to minimize risk: three to five clients gives enough data to see real results, 60 days is long enough to run a full billing cycle or two, and running alongside their current system means they can always fall back if needed.

questions.question: Before any pricing is finalized in a conversation with a prospect, what specific language must you use when discussing the price tiers?
choices: Say "final pricing" to show confidence and lock in their commitment
Always say "proposed" pricing and confirm details with Joe before anything is signed
Quote the highest tier only to leave room for negotiation later
Use the language from the Competitor Battle Cards to match the market
questions.feedback_correct: Perfect—that's the critical compliance point: our pricing tiers are still proposed, so you must say "proposed" and always confirm with Joe before anything is signed.
questions.feedback_incorrect: This is a key instruction from the course: since pricing is still being finalized, you must always use the word "proposed" and verify details with Joe before any agreement is reached. It protects both you and the prospect.

questions.question: Based on the ideal customer profile, which type of firm is not yet a good fit for the ESource tool?
choices: A bookkeeping firm with 30 monthly clients who uses QuickBooks and wants their own brand
A small CPA firm with 60 monthly clients annoyed by recent price increases from their current software
A bookkeeping firm with 80 monthly clients that needs live bank feeds and a client login portal
A bookkeeping firm with 12 monthly clients whose clients use Xero and care about data privacy
questions.feedback_correct: That firm has real needs we don't yet support—live bank feeds and a client portal are on the gap list, so honesty is the best policy.
questions.feedback_incorrect: While we're a great fit for firms with 5–100 clients, brands, and privacy concerns, we're honest about our gaps: we don't yet have live bank feeds, built-in payroll, a client login portal, or a mobile app. Acknowledge these gaps early when they come up.
